lastMistakeReview.studentAnswer: They have different units, but physically describe the exact same quantity.
lastMistakeReview.correctAnswer: Force is the interaction causing motion (measured in Newtons), while acceleration is the kinematic rate of change of velocity produced (in m/s²).
lastMistakeReview.misconception: Your answer treated force and acceleration as the same physical quantity. In lecture, Dr. Verma emphasized around 21:05 and 31:42 that Force is the cause, and acceleration is the effect.
